I am in Mwanza, and maize is my family's food. I went to school for a few years, so I can read the fertilizer bag, but cash is still tight on my own. Last season I got a FISP coupon for one bag of NPK and one bag of urea, and I am hoping for the same this year — without it I could not afford much. My plot is 1.36 hectares but I intercrop with pigeon pea and a little pumpkin, so the maize does not cover all of it. I will plant hybrid seed because the agro-dealer in Mwanza boma sells it and my neighbor got a better harvest with it last year. I also put the manure from my goats on the part near the house where the soil is tired.

For labor, it is mostly me and my husband and the older children — we do the ridging, planting, and weeding ourselves. At weeding time, when the rains are heavy and the weeds come fast, I sometimes call two or three women from the village and pay them with a meal and a little money for one or two days. I do not irrigate — the rains come in November and I plant with them. I do not buy pesticide for maize; if fall armyworm comes I pick them by hand or use ash, like my mother showed me.
